title: Withings ScanWatch ECG QT measurement leading to congenital long QT syndrome diagnosis and beta-blocker therapy
summary: Withings ScanWatch ECGs showing prolonged QT led to a KCNH2 long-QT diagnosis and nadolol for a father and daughter (Germany).
account: In a case report published on 4 July 2024 (no event dates given; publication date used), an asymptomatic 39-year-old man presented to the cardiology outpatient clinic of University Medical Centre Mannheim, Germany, because of QT prolongation recorded with his Withings ScanWatch, whose single-lead ECG recordings he had made out of curiosity; the watch displayed values such as QT 506 ms and QTc 457 ms. Genetic screening found a previously unpublished nonsense variant in KCNH2, establishing congenital long QT syndrome. Nadolol 40 mg daily shortened his QTc by 50-70 ms to 430 ms. His 7-year-old daughter was found to carry the same variant with a borderline QTc of 460 ms and was also prescribed nadolol.
purpose: The ScanWatch records a single-lead ECG and, in the version described, includes a QT monitoring function; flagging a prolonged QT interval was within what it was built to do.
system: Withings ScanWatch ECG with QT monitoring function
taxonomy_note: Chosen because the benefit was the discovery of a previously unknown inherited condition in two family members; no listed type names a health outcome directly.

ratings.reason: Two identifiable people (father and daughter) received a genetic long QT diagnosis and prophylactic beta-blockade against sudden arrhythmic death; a life-changing benefit, though no event was imminent.

ai_role.statement: The watch's automated ECG analysis displayed the QT and QTc values that prompted the clinic visit; no automatic alert is described and the report does not say who first noticed the values. Diagnosis rested on clinical ECGs and genetic testing.

evidence.citation: Rudic B, Kauferstein S, Akin I, Borggrefe M (2024). Can wearables outscore general practitioners? Congenital long QT syndrome diagnosis initiated by a smartwatch. HeartRhythm Case Reports 10(10):699-701.

evidence.quote: A 39-year-old otherwise healthy male patient presented in our outpatient clinic owing to QT prolongation recorded with his smartwatch (ScanWatch; Withings SA, Issy les Moulineaux, France).
